rationale: Crystal Mk is a small (416 lines, 7 functions, ~5 KB text) numeric kernel dominated by tight hot loops in Crystal_Cholesky, Crystal_div, and Crystal_pow, so the table favors low-cost transformations and penalizes per-iteration overhead. SUB and SPLIT get strong weights: they are cheap, low-risk, add instruction- and structure-level diversity, and SPLIT acts as an enabler that makes FLA/BCF more effective on the larger functions. FLA carries the highest SecurityGain since flattening the Cholesky and division/square-root kernels destroys their easily-recognized loop structures, but its moderate RuntimeCost and non-trivial CorrectnessRisk reflect the danger of disrupting floating-point-sensitive control flow. BCF is kept fairly strong on security but heavily penalized on SizeCost because bogus predicates inflate an already-quoted 2 KB largest function and its opaque predicates execute on every loop iteration of these hot kernels. IBR and ICALL are included with elevated RuntimeCost and CorrectnessRisk weights — indirect branches and calls tax branch-predictor-bound numeric loops and risk misbinding in this compact call graph — so the feature-driven selector will apply them selectively rather than blanket. IGV is included at middling weights: Crystal Mk has few globals, so it offers modest diversity at acceptable cost. No pass is disabled outright; instead the cost/risk dimensions let the selector concentrate heavy transforms (FLA, BCF) on the larger, RE-relevant functions while keeping SPEdriver, init, and main lightly treated.
